messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Severity: P1 — Serving cluster (rack-7) seeing sustained container restarts and OOMs across multiple worker pods. Symptoms: CUDA RESET logs, ib_rdma timeouts, increased retransmits. Auto-fallback triggered for some routes. Paging raj_oncall and sasha_infra — please acknowledge.
raj_oncall: on it. pulling logs now. which customer traffic impacted?
sasha_infra: seeing a spike in IB retransmits on rack-7 top-of-rack. if_infiniband shows lots of dropped pkts. starting grep on kernel messages for mlx5.
lee_runtime: linking to serving traces — token latency spiked ~3x at 15:12 UTC, error rate (5xx) up 14% for model-rt-prod, several containers died with "CUDA watchdog reset" and out-of-memory messages.
oliver_network: ran a quick `ibdiagnet -n rack-7` earlier — intermittent port flaps on HCA 0: Port 1. suspect fabric ECN/flow-control backpressure. attaching snippet:
```
Mar 23 15:11:02 node-072 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:83:00.0: PortState[1] DOWN
Mar 23 15:11:03 node-075 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:84:00.0: PortState[1] LINK UP
Mar 23 15:11:05 node-072 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:83:00.0: FLUSH_ERROR RDMA WQ
Mar 23 15:11:07 node-072 kernel: ib_core: QP 12345: error: RNR NAK
```
maria_support: customer-facing dashboards show elevated errors for tenants A and B, both reporting slow completions and occasional truncated responses.
raj_oncall: ok. first triage — are nodes failing all at once or per rack? seems constrained to rack-7 nodes. I'll isolate by moving traffic away from those nodes. lee_runtime can you trigger routing fallback to model-rt-prod-fallback variant for canary traffic? want to reduce load.
lee_runtime: started rollout to fallback variant for 10% traffic for affected routes. using: `curl -X POST https://console/redwood/rollout -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","variant":"fallback","percent":10}'` — logs show successful API call.
sasha_infra: getting `dmesg` from node-072 — lots of "infiniband: CQ error" and repeated "Page fault?" entries. also `/var/log/pods/.../container.log` shows repeated OOM killer entries for the serving process. suspect remote packet loss causing KV cache mismatch leading to memory pressure + retries.
oliver_network: running `ibping -S` across all switches in rack-7 — saw increased latency and packet reordering on leaf-3. config shows MTU 4096, no fragmentation. suspect intermittent switch ASIC issue.
raj_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic off rack-7 (lee did partial rollout). 2) cordon node-072 and node-074, drain workloads. 3) throttle max batch size on serving to reduce mem. 4) apply temporary iptables rule to fallback to TCP instead of RDMA for the most affected pods (quick test).
emma_ops: acknowledged for next-hand off. I'll be ready at 16:00 UTC to take over if needed.
lee_runtime: changing max_batch=8 -> 4 for model-rt-prod on live config. `PATCH /config/model-rt-prod` in progress. rollout shows success for all nodes not in rack-7.
sasha_infra: cordoned node-072 and node-074, started drain. docker reported a container restart loop on node-072 with exit code 137 (OOM). collecting `crash.log`.
```
Container runtime: oom_kill
Process: /usr/bin/serve (pid 8672)
RSS: 12.4GiB > limit 12GiB
Last log:
  ... CUDA kernel launch failed: abort() at 0x7f...
  ... NVLINK error: peer reset
```
maria_support: opening a ticket for tenant A and B and sending status update: "We are aware of increased errors and have diverted traffic; mitigation in progress. Next update in 15m." Sent.
oliver_network: switch team alerted. They found elevated correctable ECC errors on leaf-3 fabric cards and suggest cooling/port resets. Requesting permission for a scheduled port reset on leaf-3 for immediate remediation (will cause transient connectivity loss for rack-7).
raj_oncall: approve port reset if we already drained traffic. sasha, confirm drain complete?
sasha_infra: drain at 60% complete; a few pods still terminating on node-072 — should be done in ~2m. proceeding with reset after drain completes.
deploy-bot: :information_source: rolling restart of node-072 containers queued by sasha_infra at 15:20 UTC (auto-retry disabled).
lee_runtime: note — before port reset, let's disable RDMA on node-072 as a canary to see if TCP fallback stabilizes serving. command:
```
ssh node-072 "modprobe -r mlx5_core mlx5_ib ; systemctl restart kubelet"
```
oliver_network: doing that now. removing mlx5 driver will drop RDMA immediately; traffic will fallback to TCP. expecting increased CPU on node-072 until drained.
oliver_network: driver removal done on node-072. logs show IB port down. TCP fallback established for existing pods.
raj_oncall: watching metrics — repro rate on model-rt-prod down from 14% -> 4% in 30s. latency returning towards baseline. good sign.
maria_support: customers updated: tenant A sees errors drop to baseline after routing change. sending updated message.
emma_ops: taking over incident as of 16:00 UTC. summary for handoff: rack-7 fabric showing packet loss and ECC errors leading to RDMA flaps -> serving OOMs and container restarts. mitigations performed: traffic diversion to fallback variant, batch size reduction, cordoned/drained nodes 072/074, driver unload on node-072, scheduled port reset on leaf-3. Next actions: switch team to perform hardware check+port resets, post-mortem and action item owner assignment, confirm full recovery then uncordon and re-enable RDMA gradually with monitoring window.
raj_oncall: added follow-ups: - infra to validate KV cache consistency across replicas (sasha_infra) - runtime to add guardrail: failback threshold if repeated RDMA failures cause OOMs (lee_runtime) - networking to run switch-level healthchecks and ECC replacement if needed (oliver_network).
sasha_infra: creating runbook entry: "infra/rack-7-rdma-fabric-failure" and attaching logs + commands used.
emma_ops: ok let's set severity to P1 -> P2 after 30m if no regression. scheduled postmortem meeting tomorrow 11:00 UTC.
raj_oncall: closing immediate pager: initial mitigation successful. leaving handoff to emma_ops for long-term mitigation and customer comms. :thumbsup:
